_description: Battle simulator v1 (tools/nn/sim, docs/en/training/simulator.md): the numbers that are neither in a unit passport (config/nn/units.json) nor in the game's rules (config/nn/game_rules.json). Each is measured in the game or calibrated to a measurement (docs/en/training/measurements.md); `why` says which. Written by hand; python -m tools.nn.sim.check compares the simulator with the game.

step_s.why: morale rises 2 points a second before contact in every recording (+0.057 MoralePercent/s at leadership 35 ... +0.029 at 70) = one point (minimium_increment_update_per_tick) per 0.5 s tick

battle_limit_s.why: network plan: 60 minutes, the attacker loses on time

map_half_m.why: measured: routing units leave the map at |x| or |z| = 1020 m (Crossroads flat, 28 runs)

formation.why: spacing_m: a man's place across the front and between ranks for a unit WITHOUT a formation template (every unit of ours has one: config/nn/units.json spacing, the database's unit_spacings close formation of land_units.spacing - Empire infantry and lords 1.48 x 1.6 m, clanrats / clanrat spearmen / flagellants / militia 1.6 x 1.7, greatswords 1.7 x 1.75, stormvermin 1.8 x 1.9, skavenslaves 1.6 x 1.8, slingers / night runners 2.2 x 2.8, archers 2.0 x 2.1). files = floor(ordered width / h), front files x h, depth ceil(men / files) x v: the game's own formations (data/roster, 6 units, 15-80 m) give front (files - 1) h within 1.3 % (median), depth (ranks - 1) v within 14 % (wide fronts deeper: scatter); build/meleecore/spacing_check.py. Before 06.10.2026: 1.5 m for every unit (an arena spearmen fit). build/mass/spec.md read the template's numbers one row off (1.65 x 1.75 for the Empire: the next row's): the table's rows put nine floats BEFORE the key; that layout reads all 164 rows to the last byte (tools/nn/dbtables.py unit_spacings) and fits the roster depths (1.65 x 1.75 gave the Empire's depth x0.77-0.92).

turn.why: formation_deg_s: out of melee a standing formation (not walking) turns in place at most this fast (a shooter turning to its target: measured 04.10.2026, build/p3, 210 arena runs, 1 s samples: missile units p50 81 deg/s, 858 episodes; melee infantry 72; there is no game rule for a formation's turn - the database's turn_rate is a man's). A lone man (a lord) standing turns at his own turn rate: the database's battle_entities turn_rate (General 120, Warlord 180 deg/s; config/nn/units.json speed.turn_deg_s); the fitted single_deg_s 40 is gone. move_turn (1: on): a unit on the move turns towards its point at its men's turn rate (the database) and runs only the way it faces (speed x cos of the angle off, none beyond 90 deg); before, it faced the way it walked at once (an about-face in one 0.5 s step). The turning probe (build/movelords, tools.nn.charge_probe --plan move battle 1, 0.25 s samples, soldier places): spearmen ordered to run to a point 150 m behind them about-faced where they stood (each man's place along the new front against the old: correlation -0.98 - the front rank became the back; the unit's bearing turned 180 deg in ~1 s) and their centre reached the run 2.0 s after the order (0.45 / 1.1 / 2.3 / 3.0 m/s at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 s); 120 m to the side: 2.3 m/s at 1.3 s, 3.0 at 2 s; the General turned 180 deg on a move order at ~120 deg/s, the Warlord at ~200 (the database: 120 / 180), both moved off 1.2 s after the order and reached 0.9 of the run at ~3 / 2 s. A facing order in place (the simulator has none): spearmen 90 deg in 5-6 s (men moved ~8 m: the formation re-forms), 180 deg in 4.8 s (an about-face, correlation -0.97); the General 180 / 90 deg in 2.1 / 2.4 s (~110 deg/s after ~0.7 s), the Warlord 3.0 / 2.1 s (~75 deg/s - slower than on a move order and than the database's 180: OPEN). Before 06.10.2026: formation_deg_s / single_deg_s: out of melee a standing unit (not walking) turns in place at most this fast (a lord or another single entity: single_deg_s); a walking unit faces the way it walks, in melee contact.melee_turn_deg_s holds. Measured 04.10.2026 (build/p3, all 210 arena runs with 1 s samples since 30.09): missile units standing out of melee whose engine target becomes an enemy 60 deg or more off their bearing faced it within 20 deg after 1 s (median; mean 1.6 s for 60-120 deg, 1.7 s for 120-180 deg; 97 % of 160 within 15 s), (angle - 20) / seconds p25 45 / p50 64 / p75 117 deg/s - a lower bound, a turn done within the second counts a whole second; turning episodes of standing units (mv off, < 0.3 m/s, out of melee, >= 60 deg): missile infantry p50 81 deg/s (858), melee infantry 72 (23: they rarely stand and turn), lords 40 (p25 31, p75 66; 440 episodes, 2 s for 60-100 deg). 80 for formations, 40 for single entities. Before: the bearing was set at once, so a standing shooter facing away shot at once.

contact.leave_away_why: leave_away_only 1: a MOVE order leave_m or more away is a leave (no strikes, not held) only when its point lies away from every enemy the unit touches (more than 90 deg off the way to that enemy's centre); a move point through the enemy (CA's planner gives far points 55-60 m on) keeps the unit fighting (contact.hold_move: at hold_rate). The probe build/probes7 P3 (clanrat spearmen attack Empire spearmen; the spearmen walk to a point 60 m ahead, through the attacker): the spearmen dealt 213 / 317 / 521 HP at 0-5 / 5-15 / 15-30 s after contact and 29 HP/s steady (answering with an attack order 361 / 319 / 377, 21 HP/s; held 221 / 161 / 166, 13 HP/s); the simulator's leaver 0 / 0 / 98. OPEN: the game's push lane (n = 1) struck at 1.4x the attacking lane, the rule's hold_rate gives 0.5x; move_far_full 1 (a MOVE to a point leave_m or more away strikes in full, a nearer one at hold_rate as R3's 5 m lanes) brings the lane to 204 / 225 / 337 HP and 23 HP/s but rests on that one lane, so it stays OFF. Check (battles): the leave rule moves CA's planner battles 39 -> 36 % inside / skill -35 -> -42 %, the network's 38 -> 39 % / +22 -> +23 %; with move_far_full 39 % / -37 % and 39 % / +21 % (the network's same winner 135 -> 132 -> 127 of 169).

contact.attack_leave_why: attack_leave 1: an attack order on an enemy the unit does not touch, its edge leave_m (10 m) or more away, given to a formation without a missile weapon that touches a standing enemy, is a leave like a withdraw (strikes nobody, held pin_melee_s, chased, the 24 s breakoff window drops the order; leave_taken applies), in any direction. Measured 08.10.2026 (build/v2gap: 24 network battles, v2 sampled and greedy and grid_s46, game_far_sh.py, game_fresh_dist.py, game_far_dir.py): our infantry in melee given an attack on an enemy 35 m or more away struck 0.01-0.03 men/s (settled attack 0.27-0.40), moving 0.90-0.98 of the time, still in melee 0.87 of the time 10 s later; through the enemy it fights or away from it alike (0.04 / 0.03 men/s); kills come back at 25-30 s (0.34 men/s) - the breakoff window; missile units are not concerned (0.11-0.12 men/s, moving 0.15-0.18). The simulator before kept such a unit fighting in full (0.33 men/s at any distance; unit_incidental 1.0), and the v2 network learned it: 60 % of its attacking melee seconds in the game on targets 40 m or more away (grid_s46 16 %). Fresh orders, game / simulator with the rule (v2 greedy, target centre 35-50 / 50-80 / 80+ m): 0.06 / 0.06, 0.07 / 0.05, 0.12 / 0.10 men/s (before 0.29-0.33). The leave_m gap: without it the 25-35 m band struck 0.03 against the game's 0.19 (with it 0.13). The twin (the 24 battles from their recorded starts against ai_like, 4 copies): v2 sampled wins 16 -> 6 of 32, greedy 16 -> 3, grid_s46 16 -> 16 (game 0 / 0 / 3 of 8); enemy HP lost in melee 0.47 -> 0.34 (game 0.23), 0.48 -> 0.31 (0.38), grid 0.48 -> 0.48 (0.52); grid's settled melee kill rate 0.33 -> 0.32 men/s (game 0.27). OPEN: a fresh attack order on a near enemy (centre < 35 m) also strikes less in the game (v2 greedy 0.14-0.24 men/s for 20 s after the order, then 0.45-0.51; grid_s46 the same shape) - mechanism unknown (perhaps the men re-forming on the new target, perhaps who gets new orders), not modelled.
contact.friend_push_why: friend_push (battle.py; true / absent: the old rule): own standing formations that overlap are pushed apart (each half the overlap a step). false: they stand in each other as the game lets them. Measured (build/routgap/friend_overlap.py, all fair recordings, 5.3 M own pair-seconds of standing formations): centres within 2 / 2-4 / 4-6 / 6-8 m in 0.19-0.29 / 0.46-0.60 / 0.61-0.62 / 0.63-0.66 % of pair-seconds (both sides); two still, out-of-melee formations within 4 m keep their distance over the next 5 s (median change 0.00 m, 247 + 536 cases; within 4-8 m 0.00, 608 + 650), in melee they drift 0.25-0.44 m in 5 s. The network's units after the first contact: another own formation within 8 m in 13-34 % of unit-seconds in the game, 0 % in the twin with the push (build/routgap/density.py, the it3 / it4 / it5 gates).
contact.rout_pin_why: The rout's exit (battle.py; 0 / absent: off). A formation (not a lord) that begins to rout while in melee keeps its men in contact rout_pin_s seconds: its contact test leaves out the way it has run since (rpin_d), so the enemies it fought strike it on (at rout_pin_rate of the rule, from the rear, no charge; after the exit pursuit_rate) and it counts as in melee; meanwhile it gathers speed by rout_pin_speed: [s since the rout, share of its own free rout speed], linear between. Measured (build/routgap/rout_exit_game.py, contact_after.py, contact_after2.py; all fair recordings, 216 battles, 3,987 routs from melee): the game's melee flag stays on after the rout's start for p10 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 90 = 2 / 5 / 7 / 12 / 25 s (mean 11.8; 0 s in 7 %), also when no enemy targets the router in its first 5 s (763 routs: median 6 s, 0.73 for 4 s or more; chased 3,224: 7 s, 0.90); while it holds the router loses 0.243 % of its health a second, the 10 s after 0.068; against standing units in melee (build/routgap/flag_rate_all.py) 0.239 against 0.311 %/s = 0.77, and rout_pin_rate 0.83 is the share at which the twin of the 8 it3 battles gives the same 0.77 (0.43 -> 0.54, 0.61 -> 0.63, 0.90 -> 0.81; linear between; the same way pursuit_rate was set). rout_pin_s 7 = the median: the long tail (19 % over 15 s) is the chases, which the simulator keeps by the chasers' own contact. The speed: per second from the start 1.43 / 2.25 / 2.60 / 2.80 / 2.97 / 3.01 / 3.14 / 3.19 m/s, as shares of the same rout's free speed (s 15-30, no standing enemy within 40 m) 0.41 / 0.66 / 0.77 / 0.81 / 0.87 / 0.92 / 0.97 / 1.01 (2,013 routs; s 1-4: 2.31 m/s). The twin with the rule: the routers' flag p50 / p75 6 / 7 s (game 7 / 13), our losses 0.675 -> 0.663 (game 0.800), the AI's routs a unit 1.32 -> 1.35 (game 0.81), our wins 3.5 -> 4.25 of 8 (game 2): the rule is the game's mechanism but does not close those gaps. Before (off), the simulator's router left contact within 1 s (the twin of the 8 it3 gate battles: melee flag p90 1 s; HP lost in the first 5 s 0.005-0.007 against the game's 0.014; the network's routers lost 0.006 of the army's health near enemies against the game's 0.052).
contact.pursuit_why: pursuit_rate: a routing enemy is struck with every man the contact holds (no ramp) at this share of the rule, from the rear (as before), without the striker's charge (absent: off). Before, a unit touching only routing enemies struck nothing: its contact clock counts standing enemies only, so its ramp stayed 0 (a lone spear, sword or clanrat unit ordered to attack a router for 30 s, touching it all 60 steps, dealt 0 HP; build/prespec/probe_sim.py). Measured (build/prespec/specs.md item 3, build/prespec/pursuit.py, 171 battles): a target one non-missile pursuer within 12 m of its centre aims at, with none of its own units near and nobody shooting it, loses 18.1 HP/s routing (6,090 s) against 28.4 standing in melee (54,292 s): 0.64 (95 % CI 0.56-0.75); within 20 m 0.52 (0.45-0.60); every unit type about half. No charge burst: the first 5 s of a pursuit 17.9 against 18.2 HP/s later (a standing target: 33.0 against 26.6, the charge). Fitted with the same measure on the simulator's gate battles (network against ai_like, build/prespec/pursuit_cal.py): pursuit_rate 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 gives 0.15 / 0.49 / 0.97 of the standing rate, linear between, so 0.65 gave 0.64 (about 170 pursuit seconds in 16 battles: +-0.1) with the old rout_speed 0.86. Refitted with rout_speed 0.985 and the rest of batch 2 (build/batch2/run.py gap: the gate's battles, 8 copies, the same measure): 0.65 -> 0.90 (29.9 HP/s routing, 273 s; standing 33.2), 0.35 -> 0.55 (18.3 HP/s, 294 s; standing 33.5), linear between: 0.43 gives 0.64 (routers now flee nearly as fast as their pursuers run, so the seconds within 12 m are more often the first of a rout). Relative to the simulator's own melee, which is stronger than the game's (33-35 against 28.4 HP/s standing); in absolute HP/s 0.35 already gives the game's 18.1. 06.10.2026: this is the game's known bug, not a rule (CA bug report 5068 'units still not attacking while chasing enemies', reported 19.11.2024, Known Issue, still in 7.2.0: units chasing routers make no attacks until halted; by the database's rule every blow on a router is a charge, pursuit_charge_bonus_modifier 1): the measured 0.43 is kept as the game's behaviour.
contact.pin_why: pin_s: a missile unit leaving melee (leave_m) stays held this long in contact (not striking, struck), then walks out (measured 04.10.2026, build/p2/miss.py: the network's missile units in melee given a move or withdraw 15 m or more away, 254 episodes: still in melee 0.95 / 0.82 / 0.57 / 0.34 / 0.25 at 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 s; without a chaser 0.80 / 0.30 at 4 / 10 s, with one 0.92 / 0.38, build/prespec/leave.py - OPEN whether the chase explains them too). pin_melee_s: a unit without a missile weapon leaving melee in contact is held 2 s (not striking, struck), then walks out (measured 07.10.2026, the fatleave probe build/probes7/runs_melee/20261007-052219, build/probes7/leavefat.py and build/open2/leave_trace.py: swordsmen, spearmen and greatswords withdrawing from clanrats holding them, no chaser - the centre gained 1.5 / 4.6 / 9.3 m at 2 / 4 / 6 s after the order, the leaver lost health until 3.0-5.5 s (mean 4.3), 47 HP in 10 s; the twin without the hold 3.4 / 9.3 / 15.2 m, health lost until 1.5-2.5 s, 31 HP; with 1.5 s 0 / 4.9 / 10.8 m, until 3.0-4.0 s; with 2 s 0 / 3.4 / 9.3 m, until 3.5-4.5 s, 60 HP; with 2.5 s 0 / 2.0 / 7.8 m; 2 s is the nearest to the trajectory, no outcome fitted. In the game the centre moves in jerks from 2 to 6 s, the hold is the simulator's shape of it. Kept since 08.10.2026: a network (v2) used the cheaper exit, 4-6 exits a unit-minute in melee). Then it turns about and walks out unless it is chased (chase 1, build/open_battle/spec.md 2 and build/open_melee/spec.md R4): a unit with an attack order on a leaver in contact with it follows it at its own speed (stands only while they overlap by reach_m) and strikes it, so the leaver stays in contact until the database's melee_breakoff_secs window (24 s, breakoff 1) drops its order and it fights again. The game: the movelords probe (build/movelords/runs/20261006-185019): a leaver without a chaser turned about in ~1.5 s, was out of contact ~4 s after the order (the enemy's melee flag off at 4.5 s; 22 HP lost); with chasers ordered to attack it they ran 10-15 m behind centre to centre, it lost ~22 HP/s and struck nothing for 24-26 s, then fought on (the chasers lost ~20 HP/s from 26 s). 46 episodes of the network's battles (build/open_battle/leave2.py): a leaver moves with or without a chaser (3.6-4.6 m in 2 s, 10-14 m in 6 s); chased, in melee 1.00 for 6 s; unchased 0.75 at 4 s, 0.58 at 6 s. The older 'stands, 0 m' came from short episodes (the network changes its order within 1-2 s). Replaced: pin_melee_s 20 (a fitted hold of every melee leaver). A lone man (a lord) is never held (the game's lords break off melee 1.3 times a minute). leave_taken: the HP a leaving unit still in contact takes x melee (a unit without a missile weapon) / x missile (a missile unit) - measured (build/prespec/leave.py, 855 episodes: x1.23 (0.99-1.53) of the HP share a unit of its class attacking takes, missile units x0.62 (0.40-0.89)). melee_breakoff_secs: a player's account of a ~25 s order window (Steam 4416424085342483518) agrees; melee_breakoff_total_immunity_secs 10 is probably when the leaver's own melee flag goes off (the probe: 9 s after the order) - no rule of ours needs it.
contact.why: reach, lord_max_attackers, lord_splash_struck, lord_gather_s, reset_s: core_why. lord_max_attackers / lord_direction / lord_rival_others / lord_incidental: the lord swarm probe (01.10.2026, docs/en/game/units/lord-swarm.md; 3 battles, a lord standing, attacked by 1-4 infantry units from front, back and flanks, 5 repeats a layout, lords held by script so no abilities): the lord loses the same whatever the number of units (General 7.8 / 8.3 / 8.7 / 7.4 HP/s with 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 clanrat units, Warlord 6.2 / 5.8 / 5.1 / 4.8 with Empire spearmen); 4-5 enemy soldiers stand within 2.5 m of him, 7-10 within 3 m, shared by the units; an armour-piercing unit counts by its share (General: halberds alone 21.5, with one spear unit 16.1, with three 10.7). So the men striking a lord are capped in all (lord_max_attackers, core_why) and summed, split between the units by their contact; from his back or flank they hit him as from the front (lord_direction 0: the share of the database's flank/rear rule against a lone man). lord_rival_others: with the enemy lord on him too, the infantry's rate counts at this share (whole battles, a lord in melee not shot at: the enemy lord alone 14.5 HP/s, with 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 units targeting him too 18.6 / 10.6 / 15.1 / 20.4; the probe's lord-and-units trials, noisy: 0.7 +- 0.5). lord_incidental: a unit whose attack order is on another enemy strikes a lord it only touches at this share (whole battles: one enemy unit in contact, its current target another: 1.7 HP/s; him: 4.1). Front = within 60 deg of the facing (shield_defence_angle_melee 60), rear = beyond 120 deg. melee_turn_deg_s: a formation in melee turns no faster (a lord at once): measured in the 28 whole battles, infantry in melee standing turns 1 deg/s (median, mean 2.3; 20.8k seconds), a free unit struck in the flank turns 8 deg in the next 5 s (median, 653 contacts). step_m: a unit whose point is nearer does not turn to walk there (formations step back or aside facing the enemy); without it, units replayed to their recorded points stood with their backs to the enemy at contact in the pairs; leave_m: any unit in melee told to move this far or farther leaves the fight like a withdraw (0: off): it strikes nobody and is not held in place, the enemies in contact still strike it. Melee units (03.10.2026, build/gap/leave.py, melee_orders.py; the sim-to-game gap of the gate build/nn-gate/20261003-030449): our non-missile non-lord units in melee by the order in force, all 99 fair network runs with companion logs: attack 0.186 kills/s and 0.0026 HP share lost/s (129.8k unit-s), hold 0.225 / 0.0038, move to a point 10 m or more away 0.012 / 0.0045 (3.9k unit-s, moving 99 % of the time), withdraw 0.004 / 0.0038; in the gate itself attack 0.415 / 0.0035, move 0.007 / 0.0050 (34 % of our melee unit-seconds). So a melee unit moving away deals ~6 % of its attack rate and takes ~1.7x the damage; it stays in contact 97.5 % of the next seconds. The simulator kept it fighting at full rate (a move in melee was a free no-op, which the network learned to use: 45 % of its non-missile melee seconds in that gate against 0-2 % in earlier gates). The replay (tools/nn/sim/replay.py) moves such a unit to its recorded point only where that point is a move order in force: the network's units and missile units; CA's planner's and the game's AI's melee units with a far recorded point fight on in the game (the planner's: 0.17-0.29 kills/s in every direction, its point often the enemy's start beyond the enemy; build/simbatch/leave_dir.py), and leaving them made the spearmen-clanrats pair wrong. With it: the check's same winner, the network's battles 44 -> 47 of 93 (the 8 gate battles of build/nn-gate/20261003-030449: 4 -> 7 of 8; at 4 replays 4 + 1 split -> 7), the game-AI battles 22 of 26 both, mechanics 50 -> 51 of 54. Missile units, measured 02.10.2026 (build/simacc/missile_break.py, 28 game-AI and 63 network battles): the game's missile units in melee without a target and with their order point 10 m or more away were moving 45-78 % of those seconds and left melee after 10-12 s (median), against 19-36 s and 2-18 % moving for those holding near their point; the simulator keeps missile units in melee 284 s a battle against the game's 162 (median spell 15 s against 8). lord_fall.why: A lord's fall: his aura goes (battle.py: the aura counts standing lords only) and, on top, his army's other units get points by HOW he fell. Routed OFF THE MAP (gone with men left): ume_concerned_general_fled_recently -16 for fled_s, then nothing (fled: true). ROUTED or shattered, still on the field: `routed` points (0: the aura alone). rout_death_s: a faction whose routed lord crumbles to death counts him killed that long into his rout. Measured 05.10.2026 (tools/nn/lord_fall.py, 15 in-game battles, build/lord-fall/analysis.json; build/lorddeath/timeline.py): the lord killed at a fixed moment, 20 s into melee (Empire, Skaven, Vampire Counts, 2 battles each): the two idle units out of his aura and 115+ m from any enemy (12 unit-deaths) show 'general died recently' and drop -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 points 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s after, hold -16, the effect turns into 'general dead' at 45.5-46 s and the units stand at -10 from ~50 s to the recording's end (60 s); identical in all three factions. The two fighting units within his aura: -6 / -10 / -17.5 / -21...-25 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s (aura and melee on top). A lord killed while routing (4 cases) gives the same 'died recently' -> 'dead' after 45 s. Vampire Counts' routed lord shatters and crumbles (health -12 % a second), dies at 8-8.5 s, and his army gets 'general died recently' from 8.5 s, 'general dead' from 53.5 s: rout_death_s 8 (the simulator has no Vampire Counts units: config only). The same battles in the simulator (build/lorddeath/sim_fall.py: the recorded places, Empire and Skaven, the fight pairs attacking, the enemy held fearless): idle units -4.4 / -7.6 / -14 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 s after the death (game -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10; 0 throughout before this rule), fighting units net of the control -5.5 / -9.6 / -16 / -20 / -20 / -20 / -14 (game, Empire and Skaven -6.4 / -9.3 / -16.5 / -16 / -16.9 / -19.1 / -13.5; before -2 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4); the rout: idle 0, fighting -2 / -4 / -7 / -7 / -4 / -4 / -4 (game -2.6 / -3.6 / -7 / -3.3 / -0.3 / -2.6 / -0.5), unchanged. Natural falls (02.10.2026, build/simacc/lordfall2.py): in all 75 recorded lord falls of the fair battles the lord shattered with 2-50 % of his health left (none was killed), and the standing units of his army (167 unit-falls, 35 falls) changed by 0 points in the 10 s before, -1 at the fall, -3.2 / -4.3 / -4.7 / -4.8 (mean; median -3) 2 / 4 / 6 / 10 s after, -7 at 20 s - about the aura; the database's -16 / -10 on every fall gave -9 / -14 / -17 / -18 and routed 39 % of the army within 10 s (the game 21 %). So from task 20 to 05.10.2026 every fall was 0 / 0 (right for routs, wrong for deaths). The armies' collapse at the end of the game's battles is a rule not tied to the lord (collapse.why).

abilities.why: Lord abilities (tools/nn/sim/abilities.py). The numbers (active and recharge time, range, targets, effects) are the ability passports, config/nn/abilities.json (py -3.14 -m tools.nn.abilities, the game's database); what each unit owns: units.json abilities (the slots: tools/nn/sim/abilities.py slot_keys). model: the cast abilities whose effects the simulator lays on (the lords' actives). Effects modelled: scalar_speed (walk, run, and the charge speed unless scalar_charge_speed is given), scalar_charge_speed, melee attack and defence (add), melee damage base and AP (mult), charge bonus (mult), stat_morale (add, morale points). Verminous Valour's 25 m, 1 s blast (battle_vortexs) has damage 0 and AP 0 (hand decode): not modelled. triggers: when the game's AI fires an active: melee = its lord is in melee, near = a standing enemy within near_m of him, waver = a friend within range_m wavers or routs, never = not at all; friends_min: only with at least this many standing friends within the ability's range_m; default_trigger for an active not listed. Each fires again as soon as it is ready while its rule holds. Measured 06.10.2026 (build/lordduel/abilities: the active effects, nn_effects, of the game's AI lords in 139 gate battles, 85 Generals and 54 Warlords, 926 uses; a rule fits a use when it first turns true within 2 s of it; false = ready lord-seconds with the rule true and no use): Foe-Seeker and Verminous Valour in melee (fit 218 of 318 / 182 of 245, false 19 / 13 s; the old 'enemy within 60 m' 160 / 119, false 2050 / 1537 s): ~30 % at contact, ~40 % the moment they are ready again in melee, the rest a few seconds before contact (median 12 m); Stand Your Ground in melee with >= 1 friend within 35 m (136 of 206, false 16 s; melee alone 116, false 3014 s); Rally in melee with >= 2 friends within 35 m (69 of 157, false 62 s - the loosest: a wavering friend within 35 m at only 27 % of its uses; the old 'waver' 24 of 157, false 1830 s); Deadly Onslaught never (0 uses; 'in melee' held 10,588 ready seconds in 53 of 54 battles). The lone lord duels (build/lord-ai, 12 battles under the AI): only Foe-Seeker / Verminous Valour, 0-1 s after contact, again 85-86 / 77-78 s later (active + recharge); never Stand Your Ground, Rally or Deadly Onslaught. The lord's health does not change any of them. Before (an assumption): Deadly Onslaught and Stand Your Ground in melee, the speed abilities with an enemy within 60 m, Rally on a wavering friend. The network fires its lord's self-cast actives by order (Orders.ability). Passive and game-fired abilities (Hold the Line, Frenzy, Strength of the Penitent, Strength in Numbers, Scurry Away!, Single Entity) are innate effects since 02.10.2026 (`effects`): `model` lists only what this section lays on itself. Ready again recharge_s after the active time ends; at the start on cooldown for the passport's initial_s (the database's unit_special_abilities.initial_recharge, melee core 2: 0 for our lords' five actives, 3 s Strength of the Penitent, 5 s Single Entity; before: everything ready at once).
